# InputContext

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("InputContext")`

A group of `InputAction` children that are enabled and disabled together. To open a menu, enable the menu's context and disable the gameplay context, instead of checking a condition in every handler. It works wherever it is parented; by convention, put it under the script that uses it.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether this context and its actions are active. A disabled context consumes no input, so a lower-priority context bound to the same key starts receiving it in the same tick. |
| `GamepadId` | `number` | `0` | read/write | The id of the gamepad this context reads. At 0, the input of all gamepads is combined. With a positive id, only that gamepad is read, and a disconnected one reads as neutral. Keyboard, mouse and touch bindings are not affected. A context with `Sink` on consumes input only from the gamepad it reads. |
| `Player` | `Player?` | — | read/write | The local player whose character input receives this context's actions. With nil, the primary local player is used. Only a local player that is present is accepted. If the player is removed, the context's input does not move to the primary player. |
| `Priority` | `number` | `0` | read/write | The order in which contexts receive input, highest first. It decides only which context is offered an input first; `Rate` sets when actions are dispatched. Contexts with equal priority are ordered the same way on every run. |
| `Rate` | `Enum.InputRate` | `Enum.InputRate.Simulation` | read/write | Whether the context's actions are dispatched on simulation ticks or on rendered frames. `Simulation`, the default, is deterministic and is recorded in a replay; use it for gameplay. `Render` is for camera look and UI; an action read there depends on the frame rate. |
| `Sink` | `boolean` | `false` | read/write | Whether this context consumes the inputs its bindings use, hiding them from every lower-priority context. A modal dialog should sink; a HUD should not. Only the bound inputs are consumed: a sinking context that binds Escape hides Escape and leaves W available. |
